summary: Backend-only testing of iteration 6: new POST /api/company/change-credentials endpoint + slugify ASCII-fold hardening + empty-slug guards on lookup-company/company-login, plus a full regression sweep. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration6.py (39 tests) — all 39 PASS. Also re-ran prior suites test_iteration4.py + test_iteration5.py (64 tests) — all PASS. No 500s in backend logs. Company state restored to code='gestor360' / password='Empresa123' / name='Gestor360 Teste' and verified via company-login after teardown.

minor.issue: Duplicate-code check is a read-then-write (find_one then update_one) with no unique index on companies.code — two concurrent owners could claim the same code. Recommend a unique index on companies.code.

Changing the company password does not invalidate outstanding company_session cookies (30-min JWT). A session obtained with the old password stays usable until expiry. Same for code change. Low severity, but worth noting.

A code such as 'a-b' is accepted because it slugifies to exactly 3 chars ('a-b'). If the intent is >=3 alphanumeric characters, the min-length check should count alnum chars, not slug length. Currently matches the stated spec (<3 chars rejected), so reported as informational.

action_items: Optional hardening: add a unique index on companies.code to close the duplicate-code race.
Optional: invalidate/rotate company_session tokens after a company password/code change.
Code review: /app/backend/server.py is 1216 lines — split into routers (auth, company, clients, products, documents, pdf, stats).
critical_code_review_comments: slugify() now correctly NFKD ASCII-folds — verified 'Néto Açaí' -> 'neto-acai' end-to-end (change-credentials response, lookup-company, company-login with the raw accented string).
change-credentials correctly leaves company.name untouched (verified via GET /api/company after the change) — unlike setup-company which overwrites name.
Empty/`falsy` new_code ('' or null) correctly falls through to the 'Informe um novo código ou nova senha' 400 branch; symbol-only codes ('!!!','@@@','---','   ') correctly hit the <3-char 400 branch.
GET /api/company and all list endpoints correctly exclude MongoDB _id; user payloads exclude password_hash.
/api/company/change-credentials duplicate check compares against slugified code, so 'Equipe Kirius' / 'EQUIPE  KIRIUS' are all rejected as duplicates of 'equipe-kirius' — good parity.

success_rate.backend: 100% (39/39 iteration-6 tests; 64/64 regression tests from iter 4+5)

rca_of_the_issue: No product defects found. The 3 initial test failures were test-authoring errors on my side: (1) 'a-b' slugifies to 3 chars so it is legitimately accepted; (2)/(3) wrong request schema for POST /api/products and POST /api/documents (used name/type/items instead of code+description / doc_type+lines) causing 422 and a cascading KeyError. Test file corrected; full suite then green.
